items.explanation: 他 is redundant because the subject is already clear from the previous clause, so delete it; Chinese uses zero form here.
他 is redundant because the subject is already clear, so delete it; Chinese uses zero form here.
Use 不想 because it means “does not want to.” 不要 is usually used for “do not” or “do not need to.”
孟子 is the person receiving the teacher, so use 给: 妈妈给孟子找了一个老师.
It would be more natural to say 的 to link 孟子 and 老师.
Put the subject 孟子 before 跟老师. 孟子跟老师学 means that Mencius studies with the teacher.
It would be more natural to add 了 because becoming a philosopher is a completed change in the story (了completed).
